title: Base change along a directed colimit of rings: elements and zero elements come from a stage
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set, $(A_i,\alpha_{i'i}:A_i\to A_{i'})_{i\le i'}$ a directed system of commutative rings with colimit $A=\varinjlim_iA_i$ in the category of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and coprojections $\alpha_i:A_i\to A$. Let $0\in I$ and $M_0$ an $A_0$-module. For $i\ge0$ regard $A_i$ as an $A_0$-algebra via $\alpha_{i0}$ and $A$ via $\alpha_0$, and put $M_i=A_i\otimes_{A_0}M_0$, $M=A\otimes_{A_0}M_0$, with the maps $\mu_{i'i}=\alpha_{i'i}\otimes\mathrm{id}:M_i\to M_{i'}$ ($0\le i\le i'$) and $\mu_i=\alpha_i\otimes\mathrm{id}:M_i\to M$. Then (1) every element of $M$ is $\mu_i(t)$ for some $i\ge0$ and some $t\in M_i$; (2) if $t\in M_i$ satisfies $\mu_i(t)=0$, then $\mu_{i'i}(t)=0$ for some $i'\ge i$. (Equivalently, $M$ with the maps $\mu_i$ is the colimit of the directed system $(M_i,\mu_{i'i})_{i\ge0}$ of $A_0$-modules.)

proof.text: Restrict to the nonempty directed upper tail J = {i : I | i₀ ≤ i}. Equip A i = F.obj i with its F.obj i₀-algebra structure. Functoriality gives S-linear transition maps f and coprojections α, satisfying directed-system and cocone compatibility laws.

Define g : Module.DirectLimit A f →ₗ[S] colimit F using Module.DirectLimit.lift and compatibility. Concrete.colimit_exists_rep for CommRingCat gives a ring representative; move it above i₀ to prove g surjective. Concrete.colimit_exists_of_rep_eq gives a common later stage for equal ring representatives; Module.DirectLimit.of_f then proves g injective. This identifies the upper-tail module direct limit with the ring colimit.

Let E = LinearEquiv.ofBijective g. Compose (TensorProduct.directLimitLeft f M₀).symm with E.rTensor M₀ to obtain e from the direct limit of the stage tensors to R ⊗[S] M₀. Tensor induction, directLimitLeft_symm_of_tmul and Module.DirectLimit.lift_of show e of a stage tensor is α.rTensor M₀ of that tensor.

Apply Module.DirectLimit.exists_of to e.symm x for the representative clause. For eventual vanishing, injectivity of e identifies the stage tensor class with zero; Module.DirectLimit.of.zero_exact then supplies a later upper-tail stage. Directed-system identities of the tensor transitions are checked on pure tensors.

blueprint_update.statement: Let $I$ be a directed set, $(A_i,\alpha_{i'i}:A_i\to A_{i'})_{i\le i'}$ a directed system of commutative rings with colimit $A=\varinjlim_iA_i$ in the category of commutative rings and coprojections $\alpha_i:A_i\to A$. Let $0\in I$ and $M_0$ an $A_0$-module. For $i\ge0$ regard $A_i$ as an $A_0$-algebra via $\alpha_{i0}$ and $A$ via $\alpha_0$, and put $M_i=A_i\otimes_{A_0}M_0$, $M=A\otimes_{A_0}M_0$, with the maps $\mu_{i'i}=\alpha_{i'i}\otimes\mathrm{id}:M_i\to M_{i'}$ ($0\le i\le i'$) and $\mu_i=\alpha_i\otimes\mathrm{id}:M_i\to M$. Then (1) every element of $M$ is $\mu_i(t)$ for some $i\ge0$ and some $t\in M_i$; (2) if $t\in M_i$ satisfies $\mu_i(t)=0$, then $\mu_{i'i}(t)=0$ for some $i'\ge i$. (Equivalently, $M$ with the maps $\mu_i$ is the colimit of the directed system $(M_i,\mu_{i'i})_{i\ge0}$ of $A_0$-modules.)

proof.text: Restrict to the upper tail $J=\{i\in I\mid i\ge0\}$; it is nonempty, directed and cofinal in $I$, so $A=\varinjlim_{i\in J}A_i$ with the same coprojections. For $i\in J$ regard $A_i$ as an $A_0$-module via $\alpha_{i0}$; then the transition maps $\alpha_{i'i}$ and the coprojections $\alpha_i$ are $A_0$-linear and satisfy the identities of a directed system and of a cocone.

The ring colimit is also the module colimit. The compatible $A_0$-linear maps $\alpha_i$ induce an $A_0$-linear map $g:\varinjlim_{i\in J}A_i\to A$ from the direct limit of $A_0$-modules. It is surjective: every element of the filtered colimit of rings $A$ is $\alpha_i(a)$ for some $i\in I$ and $a\in A_i$, and moving $a$ to a later stage we may take $i\ge0$. It is injective: if two stage elements have the same image in $A$, they become equal at some later stage, so they define the same element of the module direct limit. Hence $g$ is an isomorphism.

Tensor products commute with direct limits, so $(\varinjlim_{i\in J}A_i)\otimes_{A_0}M_0\cong\varinjlim_{i\in J}(A_i\otimes_{A_0}M_0)=\varinjlim_{i\in J}M_i$, the transition maps being $\mu_{i'i}=\alpha_{i'i}\otimes\mathrm{id}$ (these satisfy the identities of a directed system, as one checks on pure tensors). Composing the inverse of this isomorphism with $g\otimes\mathrm{id}_{M_0}$ gives an isomorphism $e:\varinjlim_{i\in J}M_i\xrightarrow{\sim}A\otimes_{A_0}M_0=M$. On pure tensors one checks that $e$ sends the class of $t\in M_i$ to $\mu_i(t)=(\alpha_i\otimes\mathrm{id})(t)$; by linearity this holds for all $t\in M_i$.

Now (1) follows because every element of a direct limit of modules is the class of an element of some stage: for $x\in M$, $e^{-1}(x)$ is the class of some $t\in M_i$, and then $x=\mu_i(t)$. For (2), if $\mu_i(t)=0$ then, $e$ being injective, the class of $t$ in the direct limit is zero, and an element of a stage with zero class in a directed limit of modules vanishes at some later stage: $\mu_{i'i}(t)=0$ for some $i'\ge i$.
